synopsis: The corpus distinguishes European machinery standards from on-road automated-driving and consumer-testing references: EN 474:2022 is a published type-C safety standard series for earth-moving machinery in Europe and Great Britain [f2717]. ISO and IEC texts provide an international baseline, whereas EN texts can carry legal weight in Europe [f15031]. TÜV SÜD summarizes current European automated-driving regulation and ISO 34502 as requiring the virtual platform itself to be demonstrated fit for purpose [f1283]. Euro NCAP’s 2026–2028 protocols and Virtual Testing v1.00 cover on-road crash avoidance, robustness and virtual testing, but are not applicable to off-road machines [f2843]. As a separate European approval precedent, new-train approval normally includes real-track measurements of stability, rail forces and ride; these facts do not establish an equivalent virtual-approval route for off-road machinery [f14673, f1283, f2843].

relations.note: Identifies a machinery-specific EN series within the broader European standards framework.
